Market today:
The S&P 500 hit new highs, but there's a strong undercurrent of caution. A BofA CEO warned about leveraged markets after a hedge fund meltdown, and Michael Burry sees a potential 1987-style crash. For your tech/chip names, AMD sank 5% despite good earnings, suggesting specific sector headwinds.

Your holdings:
Your leveraged SOXL is down nearly 48% and SPAL is down over 56%. These are your most urgent concerns, especially with the BofA warning on leveraged markets. Remember, margin amplifies these drops. SMH is also down almost 10%.

Watch:
Keep a close eye on your leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and their stops. Also, watch how the broader market reacts to the S&P 500's new high versus the warnings of a potential correction.

Bottom line:
Prioritize risk management on your leveraged positions in this uncertain market.
plays: Re-evaluate SOXL: Your leveraged SOXL is down nearly 50%. Consider trimming or setting a tighter, active stop to protect capital given market warnings.
Re-evaluate SPAL: SPAL is down over 56% and leveraged. This needs immediate attention; adjust your stop or consider reducing exposure.
No new buys today - hold and watch. AMD sank 5% despite a scanner long setup; wait for clarity on the reasons for the dip.
